text: The Patriots are heading to Buffalo for a crucial Week 4 clash against the Bills, but they're doing so with a depleted roster: cornerback Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore have both been ruled out due to shoulder injuries, and the offensive line took another blow when guard Greg Van Roten was placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, leaving quarterback Drake Maye's protection in further jeopardy. The good news is that Maye himself appears physically sound—he insisted Wednesday that his right shoulder is fine and hasn't impacted his throwing—though he acknowledged that his early-season struggles stem more from poor decision-making than physical limitations, a concerning admission for a 1-2 team that ranks dead last in the NFL with just 9.7 offensive points per game. On a lighter note, wide receiver Mack Hollins earned the Week 4 NFLPA Community MVP award after hosting a Special Olympics Family Field Day for over 125 athletes and their families, a reminder that not everything in New England this week has been about injury reports and offensive struggles. Meanwhile, offensive lineman Matt Pryor has joined the Patriots to help shore up the line, though whether he can salvage an offense in free fall remains to be seen as the team heads to face a Bills team led by a QB in Josh Allen who has a knack for bouncing back from poor performances.
